page_hint: Ch16 §3 Worked Example, Mode 2 cloud GPU instances, H_required equation
quoted_clause: H_required = ∫_0^T N_required(t) dt + N_warm·T_warm + R_reserved; H_paid ≥ H_required ... N_required(t) is the number of hosts that must be running at time t

page_hint: Ch 16 §8 mini-case — paragraphs 'The rate comparison hides the memory geometry…', 'The honest number:…', and the closing paragraph beginning 'Request volume is not the lever:'
quoted_clause: The two hosts clear the rate comparison, not the full-context KV budget. ... The honest number: self-hosting two servers ~$40K/month all-in vs ~$104K/month API at current volume (5M × $0.0208) — a **~$64K/month saving in favor of self-hosting** ... the two hosts are sized for a ~4 rps peak — 2 × the canonical ~1.9 rps per host
observed: The mini-case proves that the two-server configuration cannot hold the KV state for the stated workload, then prices it as a viable alternative, reports a $64K/mo saving in favor of self-hosting, and finally asserts a ~4 rps peak capacity for it. The capability failure and the cost conclusion are never reconciled; the closing decision rule ('self-host if the consumed engineer's time is worth less than ~$90K/month') therefore recommends buying a configuration the same mini-case has shown to be infeasible.
correction: Add an explicit capability gate before the TCO comparison and make the cost conclusion conditional on it. Recommended wording: 'The two-server configuration fails the KV screen for 9,500-token requests (16 GB of KV against 423 GB required at 17 in flight), so the $64K/mo figure compares an infeasible option with a feasible one and is not a realizable saving; the API is the only mode that can serve this workload as specified.' Restate the geometry per replica (2 GPUs = 160 GB, 140 GB weights, 20 GB for KV + runtime) rather than as a pooled 640 GB host pool. Delete or re-derive the '~4 rps peak' claim and the 'more volume widens the gap' argument that depends on it.
acceptance_test: The mini-case must contain an explicit statement of whether the two-server configuration can hold the in-flight KV for the stated request length, and the $64K/mo saving and the 'more volume widens the gap' claim must each be qualified by that statement. A reader must not be able to conclude that buying the two servers saves $64K/mo at the stated workload.
verdict_evidence: §8 establishes '~16 GB of KV remains — 0.64 of a 9,500-token request (24.9 GB)' and 'The two hosts clear the rate comparison, not the full-context KV budget', then prices that configuration as viable ('~$40K/month all-in vs ~$104K/month API … a ~$64K/month saving'), claims 'the two hosts are sized for a ~4 rps peak' (4 rps × 8.6 s ≈ 34 concurrent requests ≈ 850 GB of KV), and builds the closing decision rule on the $64K.
fix_instruction: Insert a capability gate before the TCO comparison and make the verdict conditional: '~16 GB of KV holds 0.64 of one 9,500-token request, so the $64K/mo figure compares an infeasible option with a feasible one and is not a realizable saving'; drop or re-derive the ~4 rps peak claim on a configuration that clears the KV screen.

quoted_clause: Two systems with the same card count can differ 10× in cost per request when 3× the goodput per card composes with ~3.4× from better utilization and no idle coasting.
observed: The decomposition double-counts utilization: goodput per card already contains utilization (goodput/card = capacity/card × utilization × SLO-pass rate), so '3× the goodput per card' and '3.4× from better utilization' cannot be independent multiplicative factors. The arithmetic (3 × 3.4 ≈ 10) works, but the model behind it does not.
correction: Rewrite the bullet with a decomposition consistent with §16.4, e.g. 'Two systems with the same card count can differ 10× in cost per request: 3× from higher per-card capacity (better kernels, better quantization) × 3.4× from higher effective utilization (better batching, higher SLO-goodput per slot) — the two are independent levers, and the second is the one most often left on the table.'
acceptance_test: The factors named in the bullet must map one-to-one onto the chapter's own definitions of capacity and utilization, with no quantity appearing in both factors.
verdict_evidence: ch16 §2 bullet: 'can differ 10× in cost per request when 3× the goodput per card composes with ~3.4× from better utilization' — §16.4 defines 'effective utilization = SLO-meeting goodput ÷ theoretical capacity', so goodput per card already contains utilization and the two factors double-count the same resource.
fix_instruction: Rewrite the bullet as two independent levers: '3× from higher per-card capacity (kernels, quantization) × 3.4× from higher effective utilization (batching, SLO-goodput per slot) ≈ 10×', consistent with §16.4's definitions.

quoted_clause: TCO break-even / feasible-volume figure (referenced three times as "the figure")
observed: The figure that carries the chapter's central visual argument is referenced only as "the figure" — three times across two pages — with no figure number, while the book's own convention elsewhere on the same page is numbered ("reported with Fig 16.1"). The reader on printed p. 270 is told "the figure marks the [ILLUSTRATIVE] price band" and "the figure shades and labels that region" before any figure is reachable, and neither p. 290 nor p. 291 contains a figure at all (both pages are text-only, including the §16.4 'Measurement' list). The references therefore point forward by at least one page to a figure the reader cannot locate by number.
acceptance_test: Number the figure (e.g. Fig 17.x) and replace all three instances of "the figure" with that number. Confirm the figure falls on the same page as its first reference or immediately after it, and that the caption states what the reader should learn (break-even band as a region; feasible-volume ceiling; shaded infeasible region) rather than merely naming the diagram.
verdict_evidence: Page images PDF 290 and 291 are text-only (no figure), and pdftotext counts three unnumbered 'the figure' ('the figure marks the [ILLUSTRATIVE] price band', 'the figure marks it', 'the figure shades and labels that region') while the same pages cite 'Fig 16.1'; the figure itself is on PDF 298 (printed 278), eight pages later — the first mention gives the reader no number to find.
fix_instruction: Replace the three 'the figure' references with 'Fig 16.1' (p.270 'the figure marks the [ILLUSTRATIVE] price band'; p.271 'the figure marks it' and 'the figure shades and labels that region'), so the numbered reference appears at first mention before the figure on printed p.278.
